pumac-2014-combinatorics-b-01.prompt: A girl and a guy are going to arrive at a train station. If they arrive within $10$ minutes of each other, they will instantly fall in love and live happily ever after. But after $10$ minutes, whichever one arrives first will fall asleep and they will be forever alone. The girl will arrive between 8 AM and 9 AM with equal probability. The guy will arrive between 7 AM and 8:30 AM, also with equal probability. Let $\frac pq$ for $p,q$ coprime be the probability that they fall in love. Find $p+q$.

pumac-2014-combinatorics-b-02.prompt: A $100\times100$ grid is given as shown: the cell in row $i$ and column $j$ contains the number $100(i-1)+j$ (the first row is $1,2,\dots,100$ and the last cell contains $10000$). We choose a certain number of cells such that exactly two cells in each row and each column are selected. Find the sum of the numbers in these cells.

pumac-2014-combinatorics-b-03.prompt: What is the largest $n$ such that a square cannot be partitioned into $n$ smaller, non-overlapping squares?

pumac-2014-combinatorics-b-04.prompt: Let there be $320$ points arranged on a circle, labelled $1,2,3,\dots,8,1,2,3,\dots,8,\dots$ in order. Line segments may only be drawn to connect points labelled with the same number. What is the largest number of non-intersecting line segments one can draw? (Two segments sharing the same endpoint are considered to be intersecting.)

pumac-2014-combinatorics-b-05.prompt: Amy has a $2\times10$ puzzle grid which she can use $1\times1$ and $1\times2$ (1 vertical, 2 horizontal) tiles to cover. How many ways can she exactly cover the grid without any tiles overlapping and without rotating the tiles?

pumac-2014-combinatorics-b-06.prompt: Consider an orange and black colouring of a $20\times14$ square grid. Let $n$ be the number of colourings such that every row and column has an even number of orange squares. Evaluate $\log_2 n$.

pumac-2014-combinatorics-b-07.prompt: Let $S=\{1,2,3,\dots,2014\}$. What is the size of the largest subset of $S$ that contains no two elements with a difference of $4$ or $7$?

pumac-2014-combinatorics-b-08.prompt: There are $60$ friends who want to visit each other's home during summer vacation. Every day, each of them decides to either stay home or visit the home of everyone who stayed home that day. Find the minimum number of days required for everyone to have visited all their friends' homes.
